title: The Infinite Shore
subtitle: A map of the immeasurable
description: At the edge of a simple equation, an impossible coastline unfolds without end.
about: Choose a complex number c and start at z = 0. Repeat z ← z² + c; points whose sequence stays bounded form the Mandelbrot set. In the Julia view, c stays fixed while the starting point varies. The boundary has detail at arbitrarily fine scales, though each rendered image is limited by finite precision and a maximum zoom.
metaDescription: Explore the Mandelbrot and Julia sets, from their shared complex-plane patterns to an interactive deep zoom.

title: A Quiet Current
subtitle: Colour carried by motion
description: Stir the invisible: a small gesture becomes a river of colour.
about: A compact 2D, fluid-like model carries pigment on a grid. Semi-Lagrangian advection moves velocity and dye; a finite pressure-projection step reduces velocity divergence. The result is approximately incompressible, with grid resolution and interpolation smoothing fine detail. This is an interactive visualization, not a laboratory-validated flow prediction.
metaDescription: Stir an interactive, low-resolution fluid-like flow model and watch pigment move through its velocity field.

title: A Murmuration
subtitle: Many bodies, no conductor
description: Hundreds of small decisions gather into one astonishing movement.
about: In the murmuration preset, each agent uses three nearby-motion rules: keep a little distance, match direction, and drift toward the group. Other scenes add predators, competing groups, or visitor-placed fields. These are stylized two-dimensional agents, not a model of any particular bird species or its flight.
metaDescription: Guide a flocking simulation and explore how separation, alignment, and cohesion produce collective motion.

title: Weather, Remembered
subtitle: The shape of sensitive beginnings
description: A trajectory loops around a form it can never quite repeat.
about: A strange attractor is a bounded long-term geometry approached by trajectories in some parameter regimes. With this Lorenz setting, nearby starts can diverge while staying within the butterfly-shaped region. The path shown is a finite-step Runge–Kutta approximation; other equations and parameters produce different behavior.
method: Five nonlinear ODEs · fourth-order Runge–Kutta integration
metaDescription: Explore the Lorenz, Rössler, Thomas, Aizawa, and Halvorsen strange attractors through an interactive trajectory.

title: The Pattern Beneath
subtitle: Two ingredients, one restless surface
description: Watch reaction and diffusion draw patterns across a restless surface.
about: The Gray–Scott model tracks two abstract concentrations that diffuse and react. Feed replenishes one component, while feed and kill remove the other. This discrete 9-point simulation can form spots, labyrinths, and branching patterns reminiscent of natural forms; it does not model an organism or its development.
metaDescription: Grow spots, waves, and labyrinths in an interactive Gray–Scott reaction–diffusion simulation.

title: A Grammar of Growth
subtitle: A sentence that learns to branch
description: A handful of symbols opens into forests, ferns and impossible gardens.
about: Some scenes use L-systems: symbols are rewritten in parallel, then interpreted as drawing commands. The fern and tree instead use seeded parametric botanical constructions. These produce stylized branching forms; none simulate plant physiology or predict real growth.
metaDescription: Generate branching forms with Lindenmayer grammars, then adjust rules, growth, angle, and color.

title: Gravity Playground
subtitle: Worlds held together by motion
description: Launch a moon, disturb an orbit, and watch mass bend the paths of every neighbour.
about: Each body attracts every other with a softened Newtonian force that stays finite at close range. Velocity-Verlet advances the smooth motion in normalized scene units. Finite steps make energy conservation approximate; contacts and manual edits can also change it. Merge, bounce, and pass are simplified contact rules.
metaDescription: Launch bodies into an interactive N-body gravity simulation with velocity-Verlet integration and selectable collision rules.

title: Inside the Machine
subtitle: A little computer, instruction by instruction
description: Watch a real instruction travel from memory through registers, the decoder and the ALU.
about: This small 8-bit teaching processor has four registers, 16 memory cells, a program counter, an instruction register and a decoder. Each clock fetches one assembly instruction, decodes its operands, then commits the result through the data bus. Arithmetic wraps modulo 256.
metaDescription: Step through an 8-bit teaching computer as instructions move through memory, registers, decoding, and arithmetic.

title: Neural Networks
subtitle: A boundary learned from examples
description: Train a compact neural network and watch its decision surface move with every update.
about: A feedforward network applies weighted sums, biases, and an activation function layer by layer. Online stochastic gradient descent updates a squared-error objective by backpropagating through those operations. The color field samples the current model output across a two-dimensional input plane; it does not measure how well the model generalizes beyond its examples.
metaDescription: Train a small neural network on interactive datasets and watch its learned decision boundary update.

title: Logic Laboratory
subtitle: Make the invisible bit resolve
description: Connect a few gates and watch a question become a one or a zero.
about: Boolean gates are evaluated from source inputs in topological order. Each wire carries the source’s actual zero or one. Unconnected pins remain unknown, and combinational feedback is reported as a cycle instead of being assigned a misleading output.
method: Boolean algebra · combinational circuits · topological evaluation
metaDescription: Build and test Boolean logic circuits, including adders, multiplexers, and cycle detection.

title: Invisible Forces
subtitle: Trace the shape of an electric field
description: Move charges through the dark and make potential, direction and motion visible.
about: Each source contributes a softened Coulomb field and scalar potential; a small length scale keeps values finite at charge centers. Contours and field lines depict those fields. Test bodies follow numerical qE/m steps in normalized scene coordinates, so their paths are separate from the drawn field lines.
metaDescription: Place electric charges and explore their Coulomb field, potential contours, and test-particle paths.

title: Cellular Automata
subtitle: A world from one local rule
description: Paint a small beginning, then follow the pattern as it writes its own future.
about: On a wrapped grid, each cell’s current state and the states of its eight neighbours determine the next generation. Explore Conway’s Life, HighLife, Seeds, and Brian’s Brain. Cell age changes the rendering, while the selected discrete rule determines every update.
method: Discrete dynamical systems · local transition rules
metaDescription: Draw initial cells and explore Conway’s Life, HighLife, Seeds, and Brian’s Brain on a wrapped grid.

title: The Adder
subtitle: One sum. Every gate.
description: Watch binary arithmetic resolve through a living circuit of real logic gates.
about: The Adder builds a Boolean gate graph for each calculation. Ripple mode resolves half and full adders bit by bit. Look-ahead mode builds a Kogge–Stone prefix network from propagate and generate pairs. Every output bit, carry and signed overflow flag is evaluated from those gates; playback reveals their deterministic resolution order.
method: Gate-level arithmetic · ripple carry · Kogge–Stone prefix
metaDescription: Trace binary sums through logic gates with ripple-carry and Kogge–Stone adder architectures.

title: The Wave Chamber
subtitle: Where two waves meet, a pattern appears
description: Sound a pulse, add a second source, and watch interference gather on a dark water surface.
about: A scalar wave field advances with a damped, second-order finite-difference scheme. Coherent emitters add phase-aligned forcing; solid strokes impose a zero-flux boundary, while a graded edge sponge damps outgoing waves. The local energy display is an estimate, not a conserved total in this driven, damped model. λ = c/f is a continuum estimate beside measurements on the discrete grid.
method: 2D wave equation · leapfrog finite differences · Courant stability
metaDescription: Explore pulse propagation, coherent interference, diffraction and standing waves in a stable two-dimensional finite-difference wave model.

title: A Geometry of Light
subtitle: A ray changes course at every surface
description: Arrange glass, mirrors and lenses to guide a fan of light through a dark optical bench.
about: Rays intersect explicit line segments and polygon boundaries. Mirrors reflect direction; prism boundaries refract by Snell’s law and can produce total internal reflection. A thin Cauchy-style material law separates visible wavelengths. The lens uses the paraxial thin-lens approximation; diffraction, interference, polarization, Fresnel brightness, and lens aberrations are not modelled.
method: Geometric ray tracing · Snell’s law · wavelength-dependent refraction
metaDescription: Build optical paths with interactive mirrors, prisms and thin lenses using ray intersections, reflection and Snell refraction.

title: The Shape of Sound
subtitle: One tone. Many possible forms.
description: Build a sound from sine-wave harmonics and see its waveform and Fourier spectrum change together.
about: The displayed waveform sums the sinusoidal partials used to construct a Web Audio PeriodicWave. A radix-2 FFT shows its frequency-domain amplitudes. An optional second-order low-pass biquad filters the audio, and the spectrum applies its digital response. This is a controlled periodic tone, not a model of an instrument or room. Sound starts only when you press Listen.
method: Fourier series · radix-2 FFT · Web Audio synthesis and filtering
metaDescription: Hear and see Fourier synthesis by combining harmonics, phase, waveform, frequency spectrum and an optional low-pass filter.

title: The Living Garden
subtitle: Survival leaves a pattern in the soil
description: Follow small organisms as they search, spend energy, inherit traits, reproduce and respond to a changing environment.
about: Agents search a spatial resource field, pay metabolism costs, and convert food into energy with inherited efficiency. Above an energy threshold they reproduce with bounded, seeded trait mutations. Population caps and resource regeneration keep this small model finite. It has no predators, calibrated physical units, or validation as a real ecosystem; its patterns are an illustration of selection rules.
method: Agent-based ecology · energy budgets · inheritance and mutation
metaDescription: Explore an inherited-trait ecosystem where resource search, metabolism, reproduction and mutation shape a bounded population.

title: The Living Network
subtitle: A message finds its way through
description: Send a message across a changing network and watch packets queue, travel, fail and reroute.
about: A discrete-time packet model routes at each hop using Dijkstra’s algorithm. Edge cost combines configured latency with queue depth; links have bounded queues and a per-tick send capacity. A failed link drains queued packets back to routing, while packets already in transit complete their current hop. This is a focused routing study, not a complete TCP/IP or Internet simulator.
method: Discrete-event packet routing · Dijkstra · bounded queues
metaDescription: Send packets through a network with queue-aware shortest paths, latency, bandwidth, congestion, failures and rerouting.

title: Where Light Falls
subtitle: Follow a photon close to the point of no return
description: Trace null geodesics around a non-rotating black hole and explore the boundary between escape and capture.
about: In an equatorial Schwarzschild plane, u = 1/r follows d²u/dφ² + u = 3Mu². A fourth-order Runge–Kutta integrator advances each photon from its asymptotic impact parameter; the critical value b = 3√3M separates escape from capture at the horizon. The background sky uses the computed deflection in a thin-lens source-plane projection. The luminous disk is an explicitly artistic layer, not a radiative-transfer simulation.
method: Schwarzschild null geodesics · RK4 · strong-field lensing
metaDescription: Explore numerically integrated photon paths, critical capture, strong deflection and a clearly bounded Schwarzschild lensing projection.
